title: Impressions of the tour: audiences and Islam
summary: Carter felt they missed ordinary people and seminar time, while Berger notes full houses and the musicians' interest in Islam.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And it was very, very well received. All along the way. We met some very, very interesting people; I felt a couple of things. I felt that we didn't get to play enough of the masses, you know what I mean? The common people, that we would like to have reached, and I think that our original idea was to have done more in the seminars and things with Dr. Berger, which I was a little disappointed about. He went off on his own sometimes, and I always wanted to be along with him.
Well, in the hurly burly of the travel and you know, the messing up of airline schedules and all that, we couldn't always do exactly what was scheduled.
And the concerts had to go on; I mean, those were featured and announced well in advance. So it wasn't too easy to adjust everybody's schedule to what everybody was doing.
But no doubt, what you said --
it would have been nicer to play to larger and more popular groups in these countries. I have to admit that every house, I think, was packed. Wherever we played, it was always filled to capacity.

Oh, definitely. Definitely. Well, my feeling was that most of these people were people from embassies, they were in the diplomatic services of their own countries, and they were probably - - they had probably been exposed to jazz much more in all sorts of things, you know.
But the people like -- for whom we played in Iraq.
I mean, these were the people that I felt were getting something that was quite new to them. They, you know ...
Well, there were a lot of people like that, you see.

Yeah. In every one of these audiences, some, maybe, not as much as would have been advisable or even feasible if that was kept in mind at the very beginning. But you know, it was a big project, and you can't cover absolutely every bit of ground and every particular exact way that you want to.
What struck me about the musicians, including your-

slef, was the interest that you found in the Near Eastern life, the meeting of the people there -- not just the food, which everybody loved, or even the sites, but also the religion of Islam and the amount of reading that people did, that the musicians did, was really interesting.
